alex_privacy: FYI — we just got a DSAR from an EU user asking for deletion of all derived embeddings and any backups. They listed account id u-18872. Need guidance on our deletion/retention path and any retention exception process.

chris_infra: Thanks. Quick q: where exactly are the embeddings stored for that workload? index store vs raw S3?

alex_privacy: embeddings-prod index + we also snapshot periodic exports to s3://redwood-embeddings-prod/snapshots/2026-03-... (versioned). Snapshots are encrypted with CMK arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef12-3456.

maria_privsec: Heads-up: check litigation/legal hold first. If there's an active hold, we can't delete. @legal already pinged. Also need to record an audit timeline for the DSAR response.

katie_sre: From infra side — deleting index entries is straightforward, but S3 object versioning + snapshots mean "delete" is tombstone unless we purge versions. KMS ciphertext prevents deleting key until zero ciphertext. We'll need a retention exception if legal says keep backups but user requested deletion.

chris_infra: Proposed immediate steps (can someone approve):
1) Mark request in the DSAR tracker (privacy) and create a retention-exception ticket if legal requests retention.
2) Run index-level delete for u-18872. Example internal call:```\nPOST /internal/index/delete\nContent-Type: application/json\n{\n  "user_id": "u-18872",\n  "index": "embeddings-v1",\n  "force": true\n}\n```
3) Identify S3 snapshot objects containing that user's vectors (tagged with user id in manifest) and schedule versioned object purge (requires infra + audit).
4) Rotate or schedule CMK retirement only after ciphertext removed.

maria_privsec: Add that every action must be logged with principal and reason. We need RBAC to ensure only people with the data-deletion role can run step 2/3. Right now only devops-admin and infra-leads have access. Can we create a scoped role?

chris_infra: I can prepare a short RBAC change: new role "data-deleter:embeddings" with just two permissions: internal:index:delete and s3:deleteObjectVersion (scoped to embeddings buckets). Will create PR for policy and request approval from security ops.

alex_privacy: @maria_privsec legal replied — no active hold. Good to proceed. They want confirmation of complete removal and timeline. Also they asked about KMS: if we delete ciphertext objects, will the CMK still show activity? Any impact to other customers?

katie_sre: If we purge all versions referencing that user's ciphertext, CMK can be scheduled for deletion/disabled but only if no other ciphertext exists. We must be careful: CMK is shared across many snapshots. We cannot delete the CMK unless we re-encrypt or delete everything encrypted under it — not realistic. Instead we'll delete ciphertext referencing the user and record KMS key usage in the audit. No cross-customer impact expected if we only remove user objects.

maria_privsec: For the DSAR letter to the user, we need: what we deleted (index entries, s3 versions), when, who approved, and if anything we couldn't delete (e.g., cross-customer snapshots or immutable logs). Also confirm whether we applied data minimization rules to avoid future re-ingestion.

alex_privacy: Question: should we update our data-minimization policy to avoid storing raw text with embeddings or to avoid user-id in snapshot manifests? That'd help long-term. I'm drafting a policy proposal.

chris_infra: Agree. Short-term we should add a post-ingest transform to remove PII from metadata and store only hashed user ids in manifests. Longer-term we should avoid full-user manifests in snapshots.

katie_sre: Operational checklist I propose (tactical):
- obtain DSAR ticket id and legal sign-off
- snapshot current manifest + put in secure walled folder for eDiscovery (with access logs)
- run index delete command (record command output in audit)
- identify s3 object versions -> call purge API with justification
- update RBAC to add data-deleter role and restrict to 2 approvers
- create postmortem doc in privacy team for this flow

audit-bot: Audit event created: evt_20260320_dsar_u18872 by alex_privacy. Link: https://internal.audit/evt_20260320_dsar_u18872

maria_privsec: One more: vuln triage note — last month we had a minor vuln in the embeddings ingestion pipeline (CVE-2026-1155) that allowed metadata leakage to logs. Confirm we've scrubbed logs for this user and rotated any secrets referenced.

chris_infra: Confirmed: logs were scrubbed for ingestion job ids 3344-3352; secrets rotated last week. Will attach proof to the DSAR ticket.

alex_privacy: OK — moving forward. Approvals needed: @maria_privsec (privacy sign-off) and @katie_sre (ops sign-off) before purge. Chris, can you open the RBAC PR today?

chris_infra: On it. PR will be at https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/924 with the policy diff. ETA 3h.

maria_privsec: Approve for deletion once PR merged + audit events captured. I'll prepare the DSAR response template and include the exact deletion timestamps.

alex_privacy: Thanks everyone. I'll update the DSAR tracker and ping the user when we have deletion confirmation. :white_check_mark:
